title: Project Proposal
text:
Research Questions
1. In which majors is the GPA most affected by heavier AI Usage?
2. How can AI be used for the best GPA score?
The audience for this analysis is students who want to understand how good AI is and normal to use in their field for a better grade. The overall message is more important than the details for this scenario. So simple visualizations like graphs without clutter should work best.

Issues with the dataset?
The dataset is pretty clean as it has no missing values or weird formatting. Overall, there are no issues with the values in the dataset.
Now that we know more about the dataset, let’s do some EDA:


Code
ggplot(data, aes(x = Paid_Subscription, y = Tool_Diversity)) + geom_boxplot()









Interestingly, the tool diversity doesn’t seem to be affected by the student using a paid subscription or not.


Code
ggplot(data, aes(x = Major_Category, y = Weekly_GenAI_Hours)) + geom_boxplot()









Students in the business sector seem to use AI the most for studying, while people who use it the least are in the field of humanities.
But this doesn’t consider the traditional learning hours at all. So we might have a bias if there are differences in the total learning hours between the majors.
E.g., students of one major might use generative AI for fewer hours than others, while also learning way less in general. This would result in them using generative AI more than other majors when they learn, while the opposite is shown in the plot.
We can resolve this by looking at the percentage of AI used for learning instead:
y = Weekly_GenAI_Hours / (Weekly_GenAI_Hours + Traditional_Study_Hours)


Code
ggplot(data, aes(x = Major_Category, y = Weekly_GenAI_Hours / (Weekly_GenAI_Hours + Traditional_Study_Hours))) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    x = "Major Category",
    y = "Heaviness of AI-Usage for learning"
  )









Luckily we can see that nothing truely changes, when also considering the traditional study hours.

title: Project Proposal
text:
Analysis Plan
The most important variables I am going to use are the pre and post semester GPA, as for both questions we need to measure the students’ performance affected by AI.
For question 1, we also need the weekly generative AI study hours and the traditional study hours to measure how heavy the students’ AI usage is in percentages. To compare the majors in the first place, we need the accordingly called column. As we have 3 dimensions now, faceting between the majors is the way to avoid clutter.
For question 2, the idea is to create a model which can predict how students should use AI to improve the GPA score, given some information about the student. This will surely use most columns of the dataset.

The synthetic dataset “Impact of Ai on Students” is about the generative AI usage of students and its effects on them. There are 50000 rows representing 50000 simulated students. title: StatProg2 - A statistical programming exercise on student AI behaviour
text:
Data
The synthetic dataset “Impact of Ai on Students” by laveshjadon is about the generative AI usage of students and its effects on them. It features 50000 simulated students with 16 features. They capture various key information of the students (e.g. their major, study year & GPA score), but also how they use generative AI (e.g. which tools they use, which usecase they have & their prompting skills).

title: StatProg2 - A statistical programming exercise on student AI behaviour
text:
Results
First, we observed that heavy AI usage seems to have a beneficial effect on the grade when using it for more than half of the learn time and this is independent of the majors.
Using it much and correctly gives some outliers even a huge boost to their grade which fortifies the need of the second question.
Secondly, we have created a model which is able to tell a student how AI can be used best for them.

title: StatProg2 - A statistical programming exercise on student AI behaviour
text:
Discussion
Given the dataset is synthetic, the observations and conclusions from this research might be statistically correct, but the dataset (even though realistic) is prone to have biases which might make these findings in fact incorrect. Caution is a must.
Keep in mind that the first observation comes from the GPA change over one semester, so heavy AI usage might as well only be a short time gain or might even worsen the GPA in the long term. This data alone cannot anwser that.
But what one could certainly draw from this is that AI can help in a buisy semester.
The model is bound to have some biases, given synthetic data cannot be a perfect representation of the real word, but I believe it can still give a good suggestion, when questioning the results and building on them. However, one major flaw is that the data doesn’t include long-term effects (only GPA change over one semester). The model cannot represent them accordingly which might be a dangerous restriction.

title: Group Reflection
text:
Key analytical decisions
Describe 2–3 decisions that had a meaningful effect on your results or workflow.

Decision 1: Machine Learning vs Simple Correlation Plots
What were we deciding between?
Using machine learning or just the easy quick was with some correlation plots to find out what kind of AI-Usage is recommended for the best GPA-score.
How did we reason through it?
What can give a better insight about the causation was one deciding factor. I settled for machine learning. Honestly I just wanted to try out machine learning and it was worth it.
In hindsight, would we decide differently?
Nothing really.


Decision 2: Providing full download tutorial vs linking source
What were we deciding between?
If i should provide a full cross-language download way with a tutorial or just linking to the source where many download alternatives were listed.
How did we reason through it?
The download process is an important factor for reproducibility and even got a dedicated file in the template. Just leaving it alone with a comment “look up the source: link” felt not right, so I settled with the other way.
In hindsight, would we decide differently?
Nothing as it works fine and I think it was the best alternative.
